main_body: Tall upright stone slab (rune stele) with three cyan rune glyphs, rows 6-31
top_band: Light grey band, rows 7-10 (about 3-4 rows), with rounded corners and narrower than the body. It reads as a flat cap, not an elliptical cut face.
evidence: Down the middle column, a light grey cap at rows 7-10 sits over a near-black outline row at about 10-11. Below that is a flat dark grey face from row 11 to 31 with painted runes. The cap is a thin flat band with no ellipse, so it matches the guide's red 'flat band column cap' rather than the green ellipse cap. There is no distinct front-edge highlight and no eave shadow. The runes are painted flat on the face and are not inset. This is a front elevation with a hat, so it fails.

style.evidence: The stone has only about 3 grey steps: a light cap, a dark body and a slightly lighter left strip. The outline is a uniform near-black line around the whole shape, which gives the sticker look. The body is a large flat dark grey fill with no grain, cracks, speckle or per-stone shading. Most tiles carry only 2-4 colours, far below the cheese stall and roofed well references, which have tile scallops, wood grain and shaded stones.
